About Event

​🤖 ANYTHING APPLIED AGENTIC HACKATHON — SAN FRANCISCO

​One day. Build an agent that does real work.

​A one-day, in-person hackathon for people building agentic software. The theme is wide open — the only rule is that it has to do something. Automate a job you hate. Wire an agent into a system that wasn't built for one. Ship the tool you've been putting off for months.

​If it runs and you can show it on stage, it counts.

​🛠 SOME IDEAS

​Agents that operate real software, APIs, or infrastructure

​Automation for a task someone actually does every week

​Multi-agent systems, orchestration, evals, dev tooling

​Whatever you've been meaning to build anyway

Saturday, November 7, 2026

AIE Code Summit 2026 Hackathon
San Francisco, CASat, Nov 7 at 9:00 AM – 10:00 PM (PST)

Welcome to the AI Engineer Code Summit Hackathon!

We've teamed up with Meta, Google Deepmind, MongoDB, Subquadratic, and Fetch.ai to host a one day hackathon for working on frontier AI engineering problems, the weekend before the official summit.

Coding agents can already write code, but what happens when they must understand, finish, and judge real software on their own? Come build agents that close the gap, building systems that get measurably better with every run, reconstruct software from imperfect evidence, and verify what other agents ship before it merges.

Speakers and judges will be drawn from the top of the industry, including Ivan Leo from Google DeepMind and Mike Beltzner from Meta.

Win $11,000 in total prizes, including $5,000 for the best use of the Meta Model API!

Note: This event is fully in-person in San Francisco. Space is limited. Maximum team size is four. All attendees must submit an application and be approved to attend.

​Venture Mindset Hackathon - Reinvent Yourself in SF - builders, founders and judges: GSB/MSx, YC ...

​⏰ Doors open at 11:00 AM sharp.
🚪 Entry closes at 11:15 AM or once we’re full — come early!

​🚀 Join us on January 17 (Sat), 2026 in downtown SF for a one-day Hackathon focused on bold ideas, teamwork, and innovation.

​Participants create a clear vision of who they want to become in 10 years — not in a linear way, but in an exponential, ambitious way, similar to how venture investors think about long-term growth.

​✨ Why it matters:

​GSB/MSx alumni will see how the younger generation learns to think in true Stanford GSB style — with courage, long-term vision, and strategic imagination.

​✅ Challenge:
Create the ultimate AI sales copilot!
This hackathon is for developers, product managers, sales engineers, marketers, and AI enthusiasts who want to reinvent how sales teams work using AI.

​🔧 Choose the sales pain point you want to solve:

​qualifying and prioritizing leads,

​automating repetitive follow-ups,

​optimizing sales funnels,

​or giving teams real-time AI coaching during calls.

​🎯 The main goal is to build a working app or prototype that empowers sales teams, saves time, and drives measurable revenue impact.

About Event

NASA International Space Apps Challenge – Mountain View 2026
The world’s largest space and science hackathon returns to Mountain View in partnership with the NASA Ames Research Center. Join a global community of innovators tackling real-world challenges under this year’s theme: "The Next Frontier."
Details
Event Dates: November 14–15, 2026

Registration Opens: August 25, 2026

Format: Online (open to global participants with live streams, networking sessions, and collaborative support)

Register Here: spaceappschallenge.org/2026/local-events/mountain-view/

Who Can Participate?
You don't need a coding background to make an impact. We welcome multidisciplinary thinkers of all backgrounds:
Coders, engineers, and data scientists

Designers, artists, and storytellers

Educators, writers, and domain specialists

Space enthusiasts ready to solve bold problems

Why Join?
Work with NASA Open Data: Build solutions, tools, and creative projects using real space agency datasets.

Global Scale & Collaboration: Organized under the NASA Science Mission Directorate alongside 11+ international space agencies.

Skill Building & Networking: Connect directly with a worldwide network of technologists, scientists, and creatives.

Reserve your spot on the official event page and get ready to build the next frontier.
Official Sponsor Spotlight: Microsoft Academy! 🌌
We are thrilled to welcome Microsoft Academy as an Official Sponsor for NASA Space Apps Mountain View!
As innovators, coders, scientists, and storytellers gather in Mountain View to tackle real-world challenges on Earth and in space using NASA’s open data, Microsoft is equipping our hackers with the cloud compute, AI tools, and NASA-inspired training modules needed to take your projects to orbit.
Whether you're building machine learning models to analyze satellite imagery, predicting rocket launch conditions, or deploying a full-stack space app, check out these free Microsoft Learning Resources & Tools to power up your hackathon weekend:
📚 NASA-Inspired Microsoft Learn Modules & Paths:
Analyze Space Rocks with Python & AI: Microsoft Learn – Analyze Rock Images with AI

Day of Data – Rockets (NASA STEM Partnership): Microsoft Learn – Day of Data: Rockets

Introduction to the Data Science Process: Microsoft Learn – Data Science Process

Plan a Rocket Launch with Python & VS Code: Microsoft Learn – Learn with Dr. G

🛠️ Cloud, AI & Earth Observation Platforms for Hackers:
Microsoft Learn Hub (All Training Paths): learn.microsoft.com

Microsoft Planetary Computer (Earth Observation Data & APIs): planetarycomputer.microsoft.com

Azure for Students ($100 Free Cloud Credit – No Credit Card Required): azure.microsoft.com/free/students

A huge thank you to Microsoft Academy for empowering the Mountain View space-tech community! Let’s build something out of this world. 🌍✨

About Event

​AI Remote Hackathon (1 Week for Building)

​Build from anywhere. Take one week to turn an AI idea into something real.

​Join developers, AI engineers, researchers, and technical founders for a remote hackathon focused on building AI applications. Whether you’re exploring a new idea or tackling a problem you’ve wanted to solve, this is a chance to make time for building.

​With a full week to work, you’ll have room to experiment, test your approach, and take your project beyond the first prototype.

​What could you build?

​AI agents that handle useful tasks and workflows

​Tools that make developers more productive

​Applications for research, learning, or everyday work

​Creative projects using image, video, voice, or music

​Something unexpected—we’re excited to see where you take it

​How it works

​The hackathon is fully remote, so you can participate from wherever you are. You’ll have one week dedicated to building your project.

​We’ll share more details soon, including the schedule, participation guidelines, and how to submit your project. Register to stay updated as we announce what’s next.

​Bring your curiosity, pick a problem, and build something you’re excited about.
